question.text: What is the most common factor among all collisions in Indiana?

answer.text: Failure to yield the right of way is the most common factor among all collisions in Indiana.

teaching.text: Not yielding the right of way shows up more than any other factor in Indiana collisions. Remember: failure to yield tops crashes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Failure to yield the right of way is the most common factor among all collisions in Indiana.

question.text: What often causes crashes?

answer.text: Crashes are often caused by a driver's inattention, failure to follow the rules of the road, or both.

teaching.text: Many crashes trace back to inattention, to ignoring the rules of the road, or to both. Remember: inattention and broken rules.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Crashes are often caused by a driver's inattention, failure to follow the rules of the road, or both.

question.text: What must a driver involved in a crash do first?

answer.text: A driver involved in a crash must stop immediately, or as close to the scene as possible without blocking traffic more than necessary.

teaching.text: After a crash, stop right away or as close as you can without blocking traffic more than necessary. Remember: stop at the scene.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A driver involved in a crash must stop immediately, or as close to the scene as possible without blocking traffic more than necessary.

question.text: When must a driver move a crashed vehicle off the highway, and when not?

answer.text: If the crash happens on the traveled part of a highway, the driver must move the vehicle off the highway near the scene, unless the crash involves hazardous materials or causes injury, death or entrapment.

teaching.text: On the traveled highway, move the car off the road near the scene, unless hazardous materials, injury, death or entrapment are involved. Remember: move off unless serious.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If the crash happens on the traveled part of a highway, the driver must move the vehicle off the highway near the scene, unless the crash involves hazardous materials or causes injury, death or entrapment.

question.text: When does a crashed vehicle stay where it is instead of being moved off the road?

answer.text: A crash on the traveled highway is normally moved off the road, but a crash with hazardous materials, injury, death or entrapment stays where it is.

teaching.text: Minor crashes come off the road; serious ones with hazardous materials, injuries, deaths or trapped people stay put. Remember: hazmat, injury, death: stay.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A crash on the traveled highway is normally moved off the road, but a crash with hazardous materials, injury, death or entrapment stays where it is.

question.text: What must a driver give and show at a crash scene?

answer.text: A driver must stay at the crash scene, give their name, address and vehicle registration number to everyone involved, and show their driver's license.

teaching.text: Stay at the scene, share your name, address and registration number with everyone involved, and show your license. Remember: name, address, registration, license.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A driver must stay at the crash scene, give their name, address and vehicle registration number to everyone involved, and show their driver's license.

question.text: What must a driver do when a crash injures or kills someone?

answer.text: When a crash injures or kills someone, the driver must give reasonable help to people hurt or trapped as directed by police, medical staff or a nine one one operator, and should make sure police are notified as soon as possible.

teaching.text: If anyone is hurt, give reasonable help as police, medical staff or a nine-one-one operator direct, and make sure police are told. Remember: help as directed, call police.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When a crash injures or kills someone, the driver must give reasonable help to people hurt or trapped as directed by police, medical staff or a nine one one operator, and should make sure police are notified as soon as possible.

question.text: What should you do after hitting an unattended vehicle or other property?

answer.text: After hitting an unattended vehicle or other property, stop, stay at the scene, try to notify the owner, and call police with the information if the owner cannot be found.

teaching.text: Hit a parked car or other property? Stop, stay, try to reach the owner, and call police if you cannot find them. Remember: find the owner or police.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After hitting an unattended vehicle or other property, stop, stay at the scene, try to notify the owner, and call police with the information if the owner cannot be found.

question.text: What must your insurer file after a crash if the BMV asks?

answer.text: After a crash, if the BMV asks, your insurer must electronically file a Certificate of Compliance showing you had at least the state minimum liability coverage at the time.

teaching.text: If the BMV asks after a crash, your insurer electronically files a Certificate of Compliance proving minimum coverage. Remember: insurer files the certificate.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After a crash, if the BMV asks, your insurer must electronically file a Certificate of Compliance showing you had at least the state minimum liability coverage at the time.

question.text: What are the three ways to avoid a collision?

answer.text: To avoid a collision you can stop quickly, turn quickly away from the danger if you cannot stop in time, or speed up when accelerating is the best or only way out.

teaching.text: Your three escape moves are stopping fast, turning away if you cannot stop in time, or speeding up when that is the best way out. Remember: stop, turn or speed up.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To avoid a collision you can stop quickly, turn quickly away from the danger if you cannot stop in time, or speed up when accelerating is the best or only way out.

question.text: If a crash looks likely, which way should you steer, and how should you leave the road?

answer.text: If a crash looks likely, steer away from oncoming traffic even if that means leaving the road, and drive off the road rather than skidding off.

teaching.text: If a crash is coming, steer away from oncoming traffic, even off the road, and drive off rather than skid off. Remember: away from oncoming traffic.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If a crash looks likely, steer away from oncoming traffic even if that means leaving the road, and drive off the road rather than skidding off.

question.text: If you must hit something, what should you choose?

answer.text: If you must hit something, pick something that gives way, like brush, over something hard, and a vehicle moving your way over a still object, but a still object is safer than a head-on crash.

teaching.text: If you must hit something, choose what gives way over what is hard, a vehicle moving your way over a still object, and a still object over a head-on crash. Remember: soft beats hard.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you must hit something, pick something that gives way, like brush, over something hard, and a vehicle moving your way over a still object, but a still object is safer than a head-on crash.

question.text: How do the possible impacts rank from best to worst?

answer.text: Hitting something moving your way beats hitting something standing still, but hitting something standing still beats a head-on crash, and a sideswipe can help you slow down.

teaching.text: The ranking ends with the worst case, a head-on crash, and a sideswipe can even help you slow down. Remember: moving, then still, never head-on.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Hitting something moving your way beats hitting something standing still, but hitting something standing still beats a head-on crash, and a sideswipe can help you slow down.

question.text: What should you do if your wheels drift onto the shoulder?

answer.text: If your wheels drift onto the shoulder, do not jerk back onto the pavement; drive along the shoulder, ease off the gas and steer back gradually after slowing.

teaching.text: When your wheels drop onto the shoulder, stay on it, ease off the gas and steer back gradually once you have slowed. Remember: ride the shoulder, ease back.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If your wheels drift onto the shoulder, do not jerk back onto the pavement; drive along the shoulder, ease off the gas and steer back gradually after slowing.

question.text: What can happen if you pull back onto the pavement too quickly?

answer.text: Pulling back onto the pavement too quickly after drifting onto the shoulder can throw the vehicle off balance.

teaching.text: Yanking the car back onto the pavement can throw it off balance. Remember: too quick throws balance.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Pulling back onto the pavement too quickly after drifting onto the shoulder can throw the vehicle off balance.

question.text: How long does a car that plunges into water usually float?

answer.text: A car that plunges into water usually floats for several minutes, giving occupants time to escape through an open window while it is still on the surface.

teaching.text: A car in water usually floats for several minutes, which is your window to get out through an open window. Remember: minutes to escape.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A car that plunges into water usually floats for several minutes, giving occupants time to escape through an open window while it is still on the surface.

question.text: Should you try to open a door in a car that is in water?

answer.text: In a car in water, do not try to open a door, because water pressure makes it nearly impossible and an open door floods the inside.

teaching.text: Forget the door in water: the pressure makes it nearly impossible to open, and opening it floods the car. Remember: window, not door.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a car in water, do not try to open a door, because water pressure makes it nearly impossible and an open door floods the inside.

question.text: What are the steps to escape a car in water?

answer.text: In a car in water, remove your seat belt, open a window, free children from restraints, climb out onto the roof and call nine one one, and never go back in for belongings.

teaching.text: Escape in order: seat belt off, window open, children free, onto the roof, call nine-one-one, and never go back for belongings. Remember: belt, window, kids, roof.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a car in water, remove your seat belt, open a window, free children from restraints, climb out onto the roof and call nine one one, and never go back in for belongings.

question.text: Do power windows usually work after a car goes into water?

answer.text: Power windows usually still open after a car enters water unless the impact damaged the electrical system.

teaching.text: Power windows usually still work in water unless the impact damaged the electrical system. Remember: windows usually still work.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Power windows usually still open after a car enters water unless the impact damaged the electrical system.

question.text: How should passengers be helped in a car in water?

answer.text: In a car in water, have older children help younger ones and move passengers to the front seats as calmly as possible.

teaching.text: Older children can help younger ones while everyone moves calmly to the front seats. Remember: older help younger.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a car in water, have older children help younger ones and move passengers to the front seats as calmly as possible.

question.text: Why ride on the roof of a car in water, and when do you swim?

answer.text: Riding on the roof of a car in water keeps you as dry as possible, and swimming for shore is a last resort if help has not come before the car sinks.

teaching.text: The roof keeps you as dry as possible, and swimming for shore is only a last resort if the car sinks before help comes. Remember: roof first, swim last.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Riding on the roof of a car in water keeps you as dry as possible, and swimming for shore is a last resort if help has not come before the car sinks.

question.text: How does alcohol affect a driver, and what sets blood alcohol concentration?

answer.text: Alcohol harms clear thinking and physical coordination and slows reaction time, and blood alcohol concentration depends mainly on how much is drunk, how fast and the person's body weight.

teaching.text: Alcohol dulls thinking, coordination and reaction time, and BAC depends mostly on how much, how fast and body weight. Remember: alcohol slows everything.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Alcohol harms clear thinking and physical coordination and slows reaction time, and blood alcohol concentration depends mainly on how much is drunk, how fast and the person's body weight.

question.text: What should you do before driving if you take a medicine?

answer.text: Many prescription, over-the-counter and recreational drugs impair reasoning and coordination, so check the label and ask a physician or pharmacist about side effects before driving.

teaching.text: Prescription, over-the-counter and recreational drugs can all impair driving, so read the label and ask about side effects first. Remember: read the label first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Many prescription, over-the-counter and recreational drugs impair reasoning and coordination, so check the label and ask a physician or pharmacist about side effects before driving.

question.text: What are some signs of a possibly impaired driver?

answer.text: Signs of a possibly impaired driver include wide turns, straddling the center line or weaving, unusual speed, near misses, stopping for no reason, and driving at night without headlights.

teaching.text: Wide turns, weaving or straddling the center line, odd speeds, near misses, needless stops and no headlights at night can all signal impairment. Remember: weaving, wide turns, no lights.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Signs of a possibly impaired driver include wide turns, straddling the center line or weaving, unusual speed, near misses, stopping for no reason, and driving at night without headlights.

question.text: What other warning signs point to an impaired driver?

answer.text: Other warning signs of an impaired driver include swerving or drifting, following too closely, abrupt or illegal turns and inconsistent signaling.

teaching.text: Swerving, drifting, tailgating, abrupt or illegal turns and erratic signaling are more signs of an impaired driver. Remember: swerving, tailgating, odd signals.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Other warning signs of an impaired driver include swerving or drifting, following too closely, abrupt or illegal turns and inconsistent signaling.

question.text: What should you do first in a roadside emergency?

answer.text: In a roadside emergency, pull onto the shoulder if you can and turn on your hazard lights.

teaching.text: In a roadside emergency, get onto the shoulder if you can and switch on your hazard lights. Remember: shoulder and hazards.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a roadside emergency, pull onto the shoulder if you can and turn on your hazard lights.

question.text: Where should you place a red emergency reflective triangle?

answer.text: Place a red emergency reflective triangle two hundred feet behind your vehicle, or five hundred feet behind it on a hill or curve.

teaching.text: Set the red reflective triangle two hundred feet behind the car, or five hundred feet back on a hill or curve. Remember: triangle back two hundred.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Place a red emergency reflective triangle two hundred feet behind your vehicle, or five hundred feet behind it on a hill or curve.

question.text: How should you get out of a car on a roadside shoulder?

answer.text: If you have to get out on a roadside shoulder, exit on the passenger side after checking for traffic, obstructions and drop-offs.

teaching.text: If you must get out on the shoulder, use the passenger-side door after checking for traffic, obstacles and drop-offs. Remember: passenger side out.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you have to get out on a roadside shoulder, exit on the passenger side after checking for traffic, obstructions and drop-offs.

question.text: Are the manual's roadside emergency tips required by law?

answer.text: The manual's roadside emergency tips are safety guidelines that are not necessarily required by Indiana law.

teaching.text: The manual's roadside tips are safety guidelines that are not necessarily required by Indiana law. Remember: guidelines, not always law.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The manual's roadside emergency tips are safety guidelines that are not necessarily required by Indiana law.

question.text: What should you keep in the vehicle for roadside emergencies?

answer.text: Keep a flashlight with fresh batteries within the driver's reach, plus a reflective safety vest and a red reflective triangle in the vehicle.

teaching.text: Keep a flashlight with fresh batteries within reach, plus a reflective vest and a red reflective triangle in the car. Remember: flashlight, vest, triangle.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Keep a flashlight with fresh batteries within the driver's reach, plus a reflective safety vest and a red reflective triangle in the vehicle.

question.text: What winter supplies should you pack?

answer.text: In winter, pack blankets, extra gloves and warm hats in case you must wait for responders or a tow.

teaching.text: Winter driving kit: blankets, extra gloves and warm hats in case you wait for help. Remember: blankets, gloves, hats.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In winter, pack blankets, extra gloves and warm hats in case you must wait for responders or a tow.

question.text: What should you do in a tire blowout?

answer.text: In a blowout, hold the wheel firmly, keep going straight, take your foot off the gas without braking, and brake only when the car is almost stopped off the road.

teaching.text: When a tire blows, grip the wheel, keep straight, lift off the gas without braking, and brake only when almost stopped off the road. Remember: hold straight, no brakes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a blowout, hold the wheel firmly, keep going straight, take your foot off the gas without braking, and brake only when the car is almost stopped off the road.

question.text: What should you do if conventional brakes fail?

answer.text: If conventional brakes fail, move to a lower gear when you can, then press the brake pedal hard and fast a few times to build up pressure.

teaching.text: If conventional brakes fail, shift down when you can and pump the pedal hard and fast a few times to build pressure. Remember: downshift and pump.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If conventional brakes fail, move to a lower gear when you can, then press the brake pedal hard and fast a few times to build up pressure.

question.text: How does braking differ between a blowout and a brake failure?

answer.text: In a blowout you avoid the brakes until the car is nearly stopped, while in brake failure you pump the pedal hard to build pressure.

teaching.text: The two failures are opposite: a blowout means no brakes until nearly stopped, a brake failure means pumping the pedal. Remember: blowout coast, failure pump.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a blowout you avoid the brakes until the car is nearly stopped, while in brake failure you pump the pedal hard to build pressure.

question.text: How should you use the parking brake after a brake failure?

answer.text: When using the parking brake after a brake failure, hold the release so you can let go if the rear wheels lock, and once stopped, call for help rather than driving on.

teaching.text: Using the parking brake after a brake failure, keep a hand on the release in case the rear wheels lock, and call for help once stopped. Remember: hold the release ready.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When using the parking brake after a brake failure, hold the release so you can let go if the rear wheels lock, and once stopped, call for help rather than driving on.

question.text: Why must you never turn the ignition to lock while moving?

answer.text: Never turn the ignition to the lock position while moving in a car with a steering wheel interlock, because the steering will lock and you will lose control.

teaching.text: Turning the ignition to lock while moving locks the steering in cars with a steering wheel interlock, and you lose control. Remember: lock means no steering.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never turn the ignition to the lock position while moving in a car with a steering wheel interlock, because the steering will lock and you will lose control.

question.text: Should you switch off the vehicle while it is moving in a highway emergency?

answer.text: Do not try to switch off the vehicle while it is still moving in a highway emergency.

teaching.text: In a highway emergency, keep the engine running while the car is still moving. Remember: never shut off moving.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not try to switch off the vehicle while it is still moving in a highway emergency.

question.text: What steps help prevent vehicle theft?

answer.text: To reduce theft, take the keys, lock the doors, never hide a spare key in or near the car, never leave it running unattended, and park in well-lit, patrolled areas.

teaching.text: Take the keys, lock the doors, never hide a spare key on the car, never leave it running alone, and park in lit, patrolled spots. Remember: keys out, doors locked.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To reduce theft, take the keys, lock the doors, never hide a spare key in or near the car, never leave it running unattended, and park in well-lit, patrolled areas.

question.text: How should you park to help prevent theft?

answer.text: Parking with the front wheels turned sharply right and the emergency brake set helps prevent theft, as can an anti-theft device.

teaching.text: Turning the front wheels sharply right with the emergency brake set, or adding an anti-theft device, helps prevent theft. Remember: wheels right, brake set.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Parking with the front wheels turned sharply right and the emergency brake set helps prevent theft, as can an anti-theft device.

question.text: What should you do when police signal you to stop?

answer.text: When police signal you to stop, turn on your right turn signal to show you have seen the officer.

teaching.text: When police signal you to stop, flip on your right turn signal to show you have seen the officer. Remember: right signal acknowledges.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When police signal you to stop, turn on your right turn signal to show you have seen the officer.

question.text: What might an officer think if you do not signal when being pulled over?

answer.text: If you do not turn on your signal when an officer pulls you over, the officer may think you are avoiding the stop or are impaired.

teaching.text: Without that signal, an officer may think you are avoiding the stop or are impaired. Remember: no signal raises suspicion.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you do not turn on your signal when an officer pulls you over, the officer may think you are avoiding the stop or are impaired.

question.text: Where should you pull over for police, and what if there is no safe shoulder?

answer.text: Pull over to the right shoulder, never into the center median or the opposite side of a two-lane road, and if there is no safe shoulder slow down with hazards on until you find a safe place.

teaching.text: Pull onto the right shoulder, never the median or the far side of a two-lane road, and with no safe shoulder slow down with hazards on. Remember: right shoulder, never median.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Pull over to the right shoulder, never into the center median or the opposite side of a two-lane road, and if there is no safe shoulder slow down with hazards on until you find a safe place.

question.text: Where should you stop if pulled over at night?

answer.text: If stopped at night, look for a well-lit place such as near street lights, restaurants or service stations, and consider turning on the interior light.

teaching.text: At night, look for a well-lit spot such as near street lights, restaurants or service stations, and consider turning on the interior light. Remember: find a lit place.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If stopped at night, look for a well-lit place such as near street lights, restaurants or service stations, and consider turning on the interior light.

question.text: What should you do inside the car during a traffic stop?

answer.text: During a traffic stop, stay inside the vehicle unless the officer tells you to get out, end phone calls and turn off the radio.

teaching.text: Stay in the car unless told otherwise, hang up the phone and turn off the radio. Remember: stay in, phone off.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: During a traffic stop, stay inside the vehicle unless the officer tells you to get out, end phone calls and turn off the radio.

question.text: What should you do with tinted windows during a traffic stop?

answer.text: If your windows are tinted, roll them all down after stopping and before the officer reaches you.

teaching.text: With tinted windows, roll them all down after you stop and before the officer arrives. Remember: roll tinted windows down.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If your windows are tinted, roll them all down after stopping and before the officer reaches you.

question.text: Where should hands be during a traffic stop, and how do you reach for documents?

answer.text: During a traffic stop, keep hands in view, the driver's on the steering wheel and passengers' on their laps, and tell the officer where documents are before reaching for them.

teaching.text: Keep hands where the officer can see them, the driver's on the wheel, and say where your documents are before reaching. Remember: hands visible, ask first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: During a traffic stop, keep hands in view, the driver's on the steering wheel and passengers' on their laps, and tell the officer where documents are before reaching for them.

question.text: What does signing a traffic ticket mean?

answer.text: Signing a traffic ticket is not an admission of guilt, only an acknowledgment that you received it, and any dispute belongs in traffic court rather than at the roadside.

teaching.text: Your signature on a ticket only shows you received it; it is not an admission of guilt, and disagreements go to traffic court. Remember: signing is not guilt.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Signing a traffic ticket is not an admission of guilt, only an acknowledgment that you received it, and any dispute belongs in traffic court rather than at the roadside.

question.text: What can happen to a suspected drunk driver who refuses tests?

answer.text: A driver suspected of drunk driving who refuses breath, urine, blood or performance tests can lose driving privileges.

teaching.text: A suspected drunk driver who refuses breath, urine, blood or performance tests can lose driving privileges. Remember: refusing costs privileges.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A driver suspected of drunk driving who refuses breath, urine, blood or performance tests can lose driving privileges.

question.text: What must officers give on request, and where can misconduct be reported?

answer.text: Officers must give their names and badge numbers on request, and misconduct can be reported to their superiors, internal affairs or a civilian complaint board.

teaching.text: Officers must give their names and badge numbers when asked, and misconduct can be reported to superiors, internal affairs or a civilian board. Remember: names, badges, complaints.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Officers must give their names and badge numbers on request, and misconduct can be reported to their superiors, internal affairs or a civilian complaint board.

question.text: What are police legally required to do at every traffic stop?

answer.text: Police are legally required to document every traffic stop, including the driver's name and address.

teaching.text: Every traffic stop is legally documented, including the driver's name and address. Remember: every stop documented.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Police are legally required to document every traffic stop, including the driver's name and address.

question.text: When is carbon monoxide most likely to enter a vehicle?

answer.text: Carbon monoxide cannot be seen, smelled or tasted, and it is most likely to enter a vehicle when the heater is on, the exhaust system is faulty, or in heavy traffic.

teaching.text: Carbon monoxide has no color, smell or taste, and it gets in most with the heater on, a faulty exhaust or heavy traffic. Remember: heater, exhaust, traffic.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Carbon monoxide cannot be seen, smelled or tasted, and it is most likely to enter a vehicle when the heater is on, the exhaust system is faulty, or in heavy traffic.

question.text: What are the rules for garages and fresh-air vents?

answer.text: Never run a vehicle's engine in a closed garage, and close the fresh-air vent in congested traffic but open it on highways in cold weather.

teaching.text: Never run the engine in a closed garage, and set the fresh-air vent closed in congested traffic but open on cold-weather highways. Remember: no running in garages.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never run a vehicle's engine in a closed garage, and close the fresh-air vent in congested traffic but open it on highways in cold weather.

question.text: When should the fresh-air vent be closed, and when opened?

answer.text: The fresh-air vent should be closed in congested traffic, yet opened when driving on highways in cold weather.

teaching.text: Vent rule in two parts: closed in congested traffic, open on highways in cold weather. Remember: close in traffic, open cold.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The fresh-air vent should be closed in congested traffic, yet opened when driving on highways in cold weather.

question.text: What are symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning?

answer.text: Symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning can include drowsiness or dizziness, bluish skin or lips, headache and increased sensitivity to light.

teaching.text: Drowsiness, dizziness, bluish skin or lips, headache and light sensitivity can mean carbon monoxide poisoning. Remember: dizzy, blue lips, headache.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning can include drowsiness or dizziness, bluish skin or lips, headache and increased sensitivity to light.

question.text: How can you guard against exhaust leaks?

answer.text: A faulty exhaust can leak fumes into the back seat, so have the exhaust checked regularly and listen for any unusual roar under the car.

teaching.text: A leaking exhaust can send fumes into the back seat, so get it checked regularly and notice any new roar underneath. Remember: check exhaust, hear roars.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A faulty exhaust can leak fumes into the back seat, so have the exhaust checked regularly and listen for any unusual roar under the car.
